items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XVI, List of Answers on Terminology 84:1
items.html: It is known that the totality of the discernments that fell at the time of the breaking of the vessels are 320 sparks: eight kings, each containing four discernments, and ten Sefirot in each discernment of them, which in gematria are 320. And they divide into the nine upper [Sefirot] of each discernment, which have a sorting and are in gematria 288 sparks; and into the Malchuts of each discernment, which have no sorting in the six thousand years, which are the thirty-two Malchuts in the thirty-two discernments. And after all the worlds were sorted and corrected from the breaking, that is, before the sin of the First Man, there still remained these thirty-two Malchuts mentioned above, without any sorting, and they are what is called "the dregs of the dross of the gold", that is, the waste that remains after all the refining, in which there is no longer any use. (Item 10).
